data.name: Mary
data.gender_notes: Mary is used as a female name in christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew Miriam. Standard interpretations give 'beloved' or 'rebellious'; a popular alternative links it to mara, 'bitter'. Its root is Hebrew m-r-y-m. Mary, the mother of Jesus (Luke 1:26-38). Mary is a Hebrew name meaning “Beloved; (also) bitter; rebellious”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Mary expresses “Beloved; (also) bitter; rebellious”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Hebrew Miriam. Standard interpretations give 'beloved' or 'rebellious'; a popular alternative links it to mara, 'bitter'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mary total 21, reducing to 3. Number 3 is associated with expression, creativity and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Mary is used in Hebrew naming tradition with the meaning “Beloved; (also) bitter; rebellious”.
data.spiritual_significance: Any spiritual significance attached to Mary is interpretive and is labelled as such.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning “Beloved; (also) bitter; rebellious” is the basis of any symbolism attached to Mary; such symbolism is interpretive.

biblical_reference.note: The name Mary is prominently featured in the New Testament as the mother of Jesus.

name_in_real_life.note: No verified real-life bearer is published for this name.
